name: Resample a synthesized epic drum into a reusable sampler instrument: record 8 spaced hits on a velocity ramp into auto velocity-split layers (soften the velocity-to-amp curve so the softest layer is still audible), or record 8 slightly different hits as round-robins for fast repeats (16ths/32nds without machine-gunning), add velocity-to-low-pass (floor about 1-1.5 kHz) and small start-time jitter, and bounce a panned 4-5 instance ensemble as its own multisample
goal: Stop running several synth instances for one drum. Capture the epic drum (see the synth drum ensemble skill for the multi-instance setup) into a sampler with velocity layers or round-robins, so it can be reused across songs, played in fast rolls, and loaded into a Web Audio sample player for Polyrhythm Studio.
prerequisites: A synth drum patch (epic hybrid / ensemble drum skills)
A sampler or drum sampler that can auto-record input into layers, with velocity split and round-robin modes, a velocity-modulated filter and humanize/random start
A DAW piano roll for programming the capture notes

inputs.name: drum_patch
inputs.description: Synth drum to capture (turn off per-instance random delay for single-instance captures)

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: 'velocity' for dynamic hits or 'round_robin' for fast repeated hits

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: Number of captured hits (8 in the video)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Sampler products named in the video are mapped to a generic sampler with auto-sampling, velocity-split, round-robin, filter and humanize controls.

Steady pitch (Matt's taste): the video adds random fine-tune of about ±1 semitone per hit to reduce machine-gunning. Prefer round-robins, velocity-to-filter and start jitter instead, and keep any pitch randomness tiny (a few cents) or off.
Capture fairly dry (a little reverb is OK for monitoring) and add reverb afterwards for more versatile samples.

Web Audio mapping: keep an array of AudioBuffers per layer; pick buffer by velocity bucket or cycle an index for round-robin; scale a BiquadFilter low-pass from about 1.5 kHz up with velocity; start = t + random(0, 0.005-0.009 s).
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Set the sampler to record its input (external/aux input) with auto-advance to the next layer per hit. Turn off per-instance random envelope delay on the synth for a single-instance capture.
steps.expect: Each hit lands in its own layer

steps.action: Program 8 capture notes spaced far enough apart to decay fully (no dense 16ths), alternating a little for variation. For velocity mode, scale the velocities as a ramp from low (not too low) to high.
steps.expect: Clean, separated hits from soft to hard

steps.action: Arm and play. For velocity mode, set the layer mode to auto velocity-split and reduce the velocity-to-amplitude amount so the softest layer is still audible.
steps.expect: Velocity picks a different recorded hit at a usable level

steps.action: For repeated hits or rolls, instead record 8 hits at slightly different velocities (and random settings) and set the layer mode to round-robin.
steps.expect: Fast 16th and 32nd repeats no longer machine-gun

steps.action: Add velocity to low-pass cutoff (floor about 1-1.5 kHz, harder hits open it) so soft hits sound softer even in round-robin mode. Optionally add start-time (pre-delay) jitter, a little under about 9 ms.

Ensemble bounce: copy the MIDI to 4-5 synth instances with different pan (about 85 L/R and 46 L/R), randomness, pitch offset, snap frequency, decay and velocity curve. Sum them to one bus and capture that bus into the sampler the same way.
steps.expect: One sampler patch that sounds like several drummers (slight flams are fine)

steps.action: Save the instrument with a clear name, for example 'big tom drum synth'.
steps.expect: Reusable drum instrument for later songs

verification: With round-robin on, 32nd-note repeats at one velocity show different waveforms on consecutive hits.
With velocity mode, the softest layer is audible and clearly darker than the hardest (velocity-to-cutoff active).
Captured samples decay fully before the next one starts (no overlap).
Per-hit pitch variation is at most a few cents in the Matt-safe version.
